# Trajectory Capture by Instrumenting the LLM API Boundary

## What This Is
Start with why you'd want to train against more than one agent. An agentic model's measured capability is not a property of the weights alone — it is a property of `weights × scaffold × tool definitions × prompt structure`. Train against a single scaffold and the model can quietly overfit to that scaffold's prompt formatting and tool schema, then degrade under a different one. A generalist agentic model therefore has to be trained against many agent implementations.

The naive way to do that is to demand every agent be rewritten in the RL framework's own DSL. That does not scale past the agents you personally control, and it creates a training-only replica that drifts from the real agent.

The alternative: **trace at the LLM-API boundary.** Every agent, whatever framework it uses, eventually makes an inference call. Intercept those calls and you can reconstruct the episode without the agent knowing it is being trained. What you get back is the classic RL triple:

- **State** — a snapshot of the critical environment variables at time *t*. For a coding agent: working-directory contents, open files, prior tool outputs, the conversation prefix.
- **Action** — what the LLM emitted: a tool call, or a final answer.
- **Reward** — a quality signal on the action or on the terminal outcome.

## Why It Matters
The captured trajectory format becomes an **ABI between the agent world and the training world**. Agent-Lightning states the goal cleanly: the trainer becomes *agent-agnostic* and the agent becomes *trainer-agnostic*. That is an organizational property as much as a technical one — an agent team and an RL team can iterate independently against a stable contract.

The non-obvious payoff is train/serve skew. Because instrumentation sits on the production code path, your training data is generated by the *actual* agent, not a training-only reimplementation of it. The skew hole is closed by construction rather than by discipline.

## Key Details
- Two directions of standardization, often confused. Agent-Lightning standardizes how trajectories come **out** (instrument the runtime, emit a standard trajectory). Kimi K2 and Kimi-Researcher use an OpenAI Gym-like interface standardizing how environments plug **in** (`reset()`, `step(action) → obs, reward, done`), so adding a task means implementing one interface.
- GLM-4.5 uses a single unified HTTP endpoint that any agent framework writes trajectories into, landing in a **shared data pool**. The pool is not merely a buffer: because all tasks deposit into one typed store, you can run per-task filtering and *adaptive sampling* over it — upweight tasks whose success rate sits in the informative middle band, drop degenerate rollouts. Data curation becomes a first-class system component rather than an offline script.
- Open question the source raises and does not answer: does training against many heterogeneous scaffolds actually produce scaffold-generalization, or just a policy averaged over scaffolds that is mediocre on each?

## Tensions
This is the ABI that makes [[agent-layer-inverts-who-owns-the-generation-loop]] possible — without a standard trajectory the middle tier has nothing to pass upward. It is the practical instantiation of [[trajectory-as-the-atomic-unit-of-policy-optimization]] at systems scale, and of the decomposition instinct in [[decomposition-and-interface-pattern]] and [[interface-abstraction-for-cross-domain-transfer]]. The scaffold-overfitting worry it addresses is the flip side of [[rl-converts-agent-scaffolds-into-learned-policies]]: once the scaffold is absorbed into the weights, which scaffolds you trained on is a property of the model. Compare [[multi-agent-environment-interface-design]] and [[agent-computer-interface-design-patterns]] for the environment-side version of the same standardization problem. Capturing state as "the conversation prefix plus tool outputs" is exactly the lossy projection $\mathcal{O}$ of [[agentic-rl-as-a-pomdp]] — the trajectory records observations, not true world state.
